name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
principle: The program reads from or writes to a memory buffer without ensuring the target address is within the buffer's intended bounds. Out-of-bounds access can corrupt adjacent memory, disclose data, crash the process, or redirect control flow.
detection_signals: strcpy/strcat/gets/sprintf/wsprintf copies into char[] or malloc buffer
scanf("%s", buf) or fscanf("%s", buf) without a field width
memcpy/memmove/read/recv length argument comes from input and is not checked against destination size
array[index] or *(base + index) where index is tainted and lacks index >= 0 && index < len
for/while loop writes buf[i] with condition i <= len or no i < capacity guard
malloc/calloc/new size uses arithmetic for later copy/encode expansion without overflow and capacity checks
JNI/native/Unsafe code accesses Java arrays or direct buffers without GetArrayLength/capacity bounds checks
negative_signals: access guarded by if (index >= 0 && index < len) before array[index]
copy length clamped to destination capacity, e.g. n = min(src_len, sizeof dst - 1)
snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, ...) or strlcpy(dst, src, sizeof dst) used with actual array size
memcpy destination size is proven at least length bytes by allocation and checked return/path
C++ std::vector::at(), std::span bounds-checked access, or Java normal array access without native/Unsafe memory access
false_defense_traps: strncpy(dst, src, sizeof dst) may leave dst without NUL termination
checking only index < len allows negative indexes in C/C++
using sizeof(ptr) instead of allocated buffer size underestimates or misstates capacity
ASLR/PIE/DEP/NX/canaries reduce exploitation but do not prevent out-of-bounds access
validating length before encoding/escaping expansion can overflow after expansion
verification_focus: For every buffer read/write, is the effective offset and byte count proven within the allocated object before the operation?

consequence_chains.trigger: out-of-bounds write reaches return address, function pointer, vtable, or security flag
consequence_chains.consequence: memory modification or unauthorized code execution

consequence_chains.trigger: out-of-bounds read reaches secrets, heap metadata, pointers, or stack data
consequence_chains.consequence: information disclosure and address leak for later exploitation

consequence_chains.trigger: off-by-one loop or terminator write uses <= capacity or writes NUL past end
consequence_chains.consequence: one-byte memory corruption, crash, or control-flow impact

consequence_chains.trigger: allocated buffer size is smaller than required copy or expansion size
integer overflow wraps allocation size before copying the unwrapped amount
consequence_chains.consequence: undersized allocation followed by out-of-bounds write

patch_principle: Validate both lower and upper bounds for every index and pointer offset.
Compute required buffer sizes with overflow-checked arithmetic before allocation or copy.
Use bounded APIs with the real destination capacity and ensure NUL termination for strings.
Prefer memory-safe containers/languages or checked abstractions over raw pointers and arrays.
Treat compiler/runtime hardening as defense in depth, not as the fix.

minimal_examples.safe: char dst[64]; snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, "%s", user);
